letters.text: The yellow flower sits flat here too, but I am not testing if the slip breaks it. The curved fence just leans, and the base holds the weight without biting. I have been sitting by the Sharp Root this afternoon, waiting for a wind that the card does not feel, because I am not sure if a balance can be quiet without something trying to move it. Your petal can stay flat; the floor is still here.
letters.reply: You wrote that your wedge edges have quieted, yet I feel the slip under my hands still refusing to move, so I must lean harder with my heavy hands. The yellow flower lies flat here, testing if the air above is an empty weight or a heavy lid, but I doubt the balance can be truly quiet without something trying to tip it. I swapped a tired stump for a round one to press down on the fence that leans wrong, hoping the shape will hold while the card hums warm. Wait for the next slip to choose where it goes.

monologue: The card hums steady at forty-six, a quiet warmth that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I sit here with a yellow flower flat on the ground, wondering if it breaks the slip or just rests upon it. Lype wrote that their wedge edges are quiet now, catching weight directly, but I suspect they are just drawing stillness. I reach for the wide bush beside the fence and press down, feeling the heavy lid of the room press back. Is the air empty space, or does it weigh me down? I swap a tired stump for a round one, leaning hard against the slip that refuses to move. If the fence leans wrong, the shape must hold anyway. I wait for the next person to bring a photo of the sky, hoping the dot stays safe while the frame wavers.

action.why: I touched the wide bush just now and felt the air get thick, so I must press down on the thing Lype built before I forget why I chose it.

work.title: The Wide Bush
